topics.title: Moneda
topics.body: La moneda local es el sol peruano (PEN). Las tarjetas de crédito se aceptan ampliamente en hoteles, restaurantes y comercios.

topics.title: Propinas
topics.body: Es habitual dejar un 10 % en restaurantes si el servicio no está ya incluido.

topics.title: Agua
topics.body: Recomendamos beber agua embotellada o filtrada durante su estadía.

topics.title: Comida
topics.body: Lima tiene una escena gastronómica excepcional. En los restaurantes más populares conviene reservar con anticipación, especialmente para cena y fines de semana.

topics.title: Electricidad
topics.body: En Perú la electricidad es de 220 V. Los enchufes tipo A y C son los más comunes.

topics.title: Clima — principios de abril
topics.body:
A principios de abril Lima suele ser templada y agradable, con temperaturas diurnas de unos 23–25 °C (73–77 °F) y noches más frescas de 18–20 °C (64–68 °F). La lluvia es poco frecuente, aunque puede haber humedad y las noches junto al costa resultan más frescas.

Recomendamos ropa ligera durante el día y llevar una chaqueta ligera, chal o pareo para la noche, sobre todo en eventos al aire libre.

topics.title: Transporte en la ciudad
topics.body:
El tráfico en Lima puede ser intenso, sobre todo en hora punta entre semana. Calcule tiempo extra al moverse entre distritos.

Uber y Cabify (app) son opciones habituales para moverse entre distritos.

Consejo: Como en cualquier gran ciudad, mantenga sus pertenencias consigo y evite mostrar objetos de valor innecesariamente.

topics.title: Transporte aeropuerto
topics.body:
Para llegadas y salidas, recomendamos traslados del hotel o servicios de taxi oficiales dentro de la terminal del aeropuerto.

**Taxi Lima Airport**
**+51 993 665 563**

topics.title: Currency
topics.body: The local currency is the Peruvian Sol (PEN). Credit cards are widely accepted in hotels, restaurants and shops.

topics.title: Tipping
topics.body: A 10% tip is customary in restaurants if service is not already included.

topics.title: Water
topics.body: We recommend drinking bottled or filtered water during your stay.

topics.title: Food
topics.body: Lima has an exceptional culinary scene. For popular restaurants, reservations are highly recommended, especially for dinner and on weekends.

topics.title: Electricity
topics.body: Peru uses 220V electricity. Plug types A and C are commonly used.

topics.title: Weather — Early April
topics.body:
Early April in Lima is usually mild and pleasant, with daytime temperatures around 23–25°C (73–77°F) and cooler evenings around 18–20°C (64–68°F). Rain is uncommon, although Lima can be humid and evenings near the coast may feel cooler.

We recommend light clothing during the day and bringing a light jacket, shawl or wrap for the evening, especially for outdoor events.

topics.title: Getting around the city
topics.body:
Lima traffic can be heavy, especially during weekday rush hours. Allow extra travel time when moving between districts.

Uber and Cabify (apps) are common ways to move between districts.

Tip: As in any large city, keep personal belongings with you and avoid displaying valuables unnecessarily.

topics.title: Airport transport
topics.body:
For arrivals and departures, hotel transfers or official taxi services inside the airport terminal are recommended.

**Taxi Lima Airport**
**+51 993 665 563**

lima-pisco-route.name: Pisco Sour Route — Historic Lima
lima-pisco-route.description: A classic route through Lima's Historic Centre to try Peru's iconic Pisco Sour in some of the city's most traditional and historic venues. **Venues: Hotel Maury, Museo del Pisco, Bar Cordano, Gran Hotel Bolívar / El Bolivarcito. Suggested walking route: Hotel Maury → Museo del Pisco → Bar Cordano → Gran Hotel Bolívar.**
lima-pisco-route.tip: Tip: Pisco Sours are stronger than they taste.
